solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: back tells us the little word is is to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
an animal's hide is its skin

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher reports a finch spotted behind the hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns IS into SI; 'hide' looks like a birdwatcher's shelter but is the noun for an animal's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: This small yellow-green songbird is a member of the finch family.

parts.note: a charm is a magic spell
abroad means out and about, away from home

explanation.surface: A traveller's magic charm makes things clear.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb meaning to explain explicitly, leaving no room for doubt.

indicators.note: into places the cricket letter inside the word for dregs

parts.note: scum is the worthless residue or lowest element
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: The lowest elements of society charge into a riotous mob.
explanation.definitionFit: A jostling, disordered mass of people is called this, from rugby's tight huddle.

clue.text: Being stupid, I initially doubted short Greek character in charge

indicators.note: initially takes just the opening letter of doubted
short means the Greek letter loses its final letter

parts.note: iota is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone admits they were foolish to doubt a short Greek in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts IOTA to IOT. 'Being' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym describing behaviour that is foolish or senseless.

parts.note: a beef is slang for a complaint or quarrel
being up means in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: Someone strengthens their case in a student debate.
explanation.walkthrough: To be UP is the British idiom for being at university, as in 'up at Oxford'.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb meaning to strengthen or make more substantial, a direct synonym.

parts.note: extra means additional or other

explanation.surface: Someone is taken out of a second courtroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to pull out or withdraw something from where it sits.

clue.text: Force to move from vault, gallons having been imbibed

indicators.note: imbibed means drunk in, so the letter for gallons is swallowed by the word from

parts.note: a vault is an arched roof, an arch

explanation.surface: Gallons were drunk before someone was forced from a vaulted cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having been imbibed' puts G inside FROM. 'vault' looks like a jump but is an arched ceiling.
explanation.definitionFit: To march someone along forcibly, holding their arms, is to compel them to move.

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the attempt goes under the friend

parts.note: a pal is a friend
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A half-hearted effort to back up a mate.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'to support' puts TRY underneath PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable in the sense of meagre or pitifully small.

clue.text: Head of lyceum getting paid for knowledge

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, here of lyceum

parts.note: earning means receiving payment for work

explanation.surface: The principal of a school is paid for what they know.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of' looks like a school's head teacher but only takes the first letter of 'lyceum'.
explanation.definitionFit: Scholarship acquired through study is a synonym for knowledge.

clue.text: Fall in and get carried away?

definitions.meaning: to topple from a boat into the water

explanation.definitionFit: Literally to drop over a ship's side; figuratively to be wildly excessive in enthusiasm.

clue.text: Couple carry on producing a type of wool

parts.note: a couple is two of something
to ply a trade is to carry it on

explanation.surface: A pair keep knitting, making a certain yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: Yarn made of two twisted strands is a common kind of knitting wool.

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: plump means chubby or round in shape

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit is nearly spherical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' removes the last letter of PLUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A stone fruit with purple or yellow skin, an example of the class.

clue.text: Hour in steam room relaxed former Lord Chancellor

indicators.note: relaxed suggests the letters are loosened and set out in a new order

explanation.surface: An hour spent unwinding in a sauna.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudor statesman and author of Utopia served Henry VIII as Lord Chancellor before his execution.

clue.text: Exposed cult joined by rank and file in government industries

parts.note: something exposed is out in public view
a cult is a religious sect
OR stands for other ranks, the ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A sect is unmasked after enlisting ordinary workers in nationalised industry.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, 'other ranks', is the military abbreviation for enlisted soldiers below officer level.
explanation.definitionFit: The part of the economy owned or run by the state includes nationalised industries.

clue.text: Bookkeeper's sign — managed to get hold of one

definitions.note: the definition is the bookkeeper, with 's standing for is

parts.note: Libra is a sign of the zodiac

indicators.note: getting hold of means grasping, so the word for managed encloses the numeral

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An accountant's star sign helps them seize something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bookkeeper' looks like an accountant but means one who keeps books in a library; its 's stands for 'is'. 'to get hold of' puts I inside RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A person in charge of a library's books literally keeps them.

clue.text: Without payment, worker shows ability to make own decisions

parts.note: free means costing nothing
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: An unpaid labourer shows independence.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being given a free hand means having liberty to act as one sees fit.

indicators.note: in places the furniture word inside the word for supporters

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it, so seconds are backers
a settle is a high-backed wooden bench

explanation.surface: Members of Parliament take their places in moments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settle' looks like a verb but is the old wooden seat; 'seconds' looks like time but means supporters. Backbenchers are MPs without ministerial office, who sit behind the front bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary members of Parliament without government posts are a subset of all members.

parts.note: a draw is an attraction, and a catch is a desirable prize
a performer is on, onstage

explanation.surface: An attraction is on stage and becoming a hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb meaning to become fashionable or widely adopted.

clue.text: In the minority? Very much so!

definitions.meaning: fewer than half of a group
an emphatic yes in British colloquial speech

explanation.definitionFit: Literally less than fifty per cent; as British slang an emphatic agreement meaning absolutely.

indicators.note: across means the decay word stretches over either side of the vehicle

parts.note: mould is a form of rot
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: Fungus spreads over a car built to last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mould' looks like a shaping verb, but it is the noun for fungal decay.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective synonym describing something strong, stout and well made.

clue.text: A lot to say, possibly, after end of meal and show of patriotism

indicators.note: after places the rearranged phrase behind the single letter
the end of a word is its closing letter, here of meal
possibly signals the phrase could be rearranged into something else

explanation.surface: After-dinner speeches and patriotic displays run long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A LOT TO SAY into OYALTOAST, set after L. A loyal toast is the British custom of drinking to the monarch at the close of a formal dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinking to the sovereign's health at a dinner is a ritual expression of allegiance.

definitions.meaning: a single stride taken while walking
a phase or point in a progression

explanation.definitionFit: A stride is one pace; a phase in a process is a stage, both senses of the word.

parts.note: fit means capable, able

explanation.surface: A fur coat is a snug fit.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelt of a small dark-furred mammal prized for luxurious coats.

clue.text: One feeding Norwegian painter in German city

indicators.note: feeding means putting one thing into another, here the numeral into the painter

parts.note: Edvard Munch painted The Scream
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone feeds a Norwegian artist while in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bavarian capital is a major city in southern Germany.

clue.text: Lazy type, unfeeling, on strike repeatedly

parts.note: a numb limb is dead, without sensation
to beat is to hit again and again

explanation.surface: A layabout, quite callous, keeps hitting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for an idle, feckless person who avoids work or debts.

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the shelter word surrounds the article

parts.note: a tepee is a conical tent
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone living in a wigwam keeps a written piece there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penning' looks like writing, but here it means shutting in, as sheep are penned.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who rents and lives in a property occupies it.

parts.note: food that has gone bad is off
an end is an outcome or result

explanation.surface: A poor outcome causes pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset someone's feelings is to wound them emotionally, a verb synonym.
